title: Acquisition readiness and evidence handoff for private deployments
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Purpose
-------
This handbook defines the minimum evidence package, export procedures, and handoff protocol Redwood will produce for private (VPC and on-prem) deployments in the event of an acquisition, divestiture, or similar corporate transaction. The goal is to enable safe, auditable transfer of operational, security, and compliance artifacts while preserving customer confidentiality and meeting legal discovery requirements.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Scope: All private deployment modes: VPC-hosted private tenants and on-prem / air-gapped installations managed by Redwood or operators with an ongoing handback contract.
- Audience: Security, Legal, Finance, Platform Operations (Operator), Customer Success, and the acquisition integration team.

Key principles
--------------
- Minimal exposure: deliver only the artifacts required by the transaction and agreed contracts.
- Auditability: every exported artifact must be accompanied by provenance metadata and a chain-of-custody record.
- Reproducibility: provide scripts and checksums so recipients can verify integrity of evidence bundles.
- Customer protection: redact or separate customer-identifying data unless the contract authorizes transfer.

High-level handoff phases
------------------------
1. Pre-handoff planning (legal + security signoff).
2. Evidence collection and packaging (operators run approved scripts).
3. Redaction and separation of customer PII (data team assisted).
4. Evidence verification and checksum signing (security).
5. Transfer with chain-of-custody and acceptance signoff (legal + recipient).

Pre-handoff planning checklist (required approvals)
--------------------------------------------------
- Legal: signed MOU or data transfer agreement specifying scope and permitted artifacts.
- Customer Success: identify customers affected and confirm consent or contract provisions.
- Security: approved export plan and temporary access policy.
- Finance: approved cost estimate for operator time and storage egress.
- Product: list of model versions and feature flags that must be included.

Evidence package index (minimum required artifacts)
--------------------------------------------------
Note: artifacts are grouped. For each artifact supply format, owner, recommended retention, and redaction guidance.

Artifact | Format | Owner | Retention | Redaction guidance
---|---|---|---|---
Service configuration snapshot (control plane) | YAML / JSON (tar.gz) | Platform Ops | 2 years | None (config only)
Runtime topology and GPU allocation | CSV + architecture diagram PNG | Platform Ops | 2 years | None
SLO/SLA definitions and current error budget state | markdown + CSV metrics | Reliability (SRE) | 2 years | None
Operational runbooks & operator playbooks | markdown | Platform Ops | 5 years | Remove on-call phone numbers unless required
Model artifacts (signed model manifests, checksums) | manifest.json + signatures | Applied ML | 3 years | Remove customer-proprietary models (per contract)
KV-cache snapshot manifest (not content) | JSON manifest with keys_count, shard map | Runtime | 1 year | Do not include cached user payloads
Telemetry summary and aggregated metrics | Parquet + README | Observability | 3 years | Provide only aggregated metrics; remove PII-level traces
Audit logs (authentication, config changes) | WORM log bundle (gz) | Security | 7 years | Mask personal identifiers unless required by law
Cryptographic key inventory and KMS event log | CSV + event log | Security | 7 years | Keys themselves are NOT exported; only metadata and rotation events
SBOM for runtime images | SPDX / CycloneDX | Eng Packaging | 5 years | None
Compliance evidence pack (pen test, compliance reports) | PDF bundle | Compliance | 7 years | Sensitive customer test artifacts separated
Legal and contract bundle | PDF | Finance-Legal | 10 years | None

Export and packaging procedures (operator steps)
------------------------------------------------
1. Create a new evidence workspace in a hardened S3 bucket or air-gapped storage: redwood-evidence/<transaction-id>/<timestamp>. Access restricted to security+legal.
2. Run configuration snapshot script (examples below). Store: configs.tar.gz and manifest.json.
3. Generate telemetry aggregates for the requested window (default last 90 days). Verify aggregation reduces cardinality to remove per-customer traces.
4. Collect runbooks and release notes from the docs repo at the tagged release. Include commit SHAs.
5. Produce a non-exportable listing of KV-cache sizes and shard maps (counts only). Do NOT export cache contents.
6. Produce signed checksums (SHA-256) for every artifact. Sign with an internal evidence-signing key.
7. Produce a chain-of-custody record capturing operator identity, UTC timestamps, and actions performed.
8. Notify Security and Legal to run verification checklist and apply final approvals.

Example scripts and CLI snippets
-------------------------------
# snapshot control plane configuration
$ ./scripts/export-configs.sh --workspace redwood-evidence/txn-1234 --output configs.tar.gz

# generate telemetry aggregates (90d)
$ python tools/telemetry_aggregator.py --start 2026-02-01 --end 2026-04-01 --out telemetry-90d.parquet --aggregate-by route,model --no-raw-traces

# sign artifacts
$ sha256sum configs.tar.gz | tee configs.sha256
$ gpg --default-key redwood-evidence@redwood.ai --detach-sign configs.sha256

Redaction and separation rules
------------------------------
- PII and customer identifiers must be either redacted or extracted into a separate, access-controlled "customer-sensitive" bundle. Only Legal may authorize inclusion.
- Aggregated telemetry should be at 5+ customers per bucket for any split dimension; otherwise merge into the next coarser dimension.
- Audit logs that include user IDs must be redacted to an anonymized identifier mapping preserved only in an internal key-value table if required.

Acceptance signoff and transfer protocol
---------------------------------------
1. Recipient executes verification script on the bundle using provided checksums and GPG signatures.
2. Security performs a fresh signature verification and confirms artifact completeness against manifest.json.
3. Legal confirms contract-aligned scope and signs acceptance document.
4. Transfer occurs via one of: - encrypted S3 share with strict IAM, - signed physical hard drive via bonded courier (for air-gapped sites), or - secure file transfer with mandatory client cert auth.
5. Chain-of-custody form is finalized with both parties' signatures and stored in the evidence workspace.

Post-handoff validation and expiration
-------------------------------------
- Recipient must run acceptance tests specified in the evidence README within 14 days.
- Redwood retains copies of the evidence workspace for a configurable retention period based on transaction terms (default 90 days) before automated secure deletion unless legal requires longer.
- If the recipient discovers missing artifacts, they must open an evidence-issues ticket referencing the transaction id; Security and Platform Ops will respond within the agreed SLA (default 5 business days).

Owner and responsibility matrix
------------------------------
Area | Primary owner | Backup owner | Escalation contact
---|---|---|---
Evidence orchestration | Platform Ops | Runtime team | oncall-platform@redwood.ai
Telemetry aggregation | Observability | SRE | telemetry@redwood.ai
Redaction & Data separation | Data Privacy | Security | privacy@redwood.ai
Cryptographic signing | Security | Eng Packaging | sigops@redwood.ai
Legal acceptance | Finance-Legal | General Counsel | legal@redwood.ai

Common risk scenarios and mitigations
------------------------------------
- Risk: Customer objects to transfer of certain artifacts. Mitigation: isolate customer-specific artifacts into a separate package and obtain explicit written consent or court order before release.
- Risk: Evidence bundle fails verification. Mitigation: maintain immutable copies in WORM storage for fast re-export; require operator to re-run collection under supervision.
- Risk: KMS keys exposure. Mitigation: never export private keys; export only metadata and rotation events.

Templates and attachments (appendix)
----------------------------------
- Chain-of-custody template (CSV)
- Evidence manifest schema (manifest.json.example)
- Verification script (bash)
- Acceptance signoff PDF template

Appendix A: manifest.json example
--------------------------------
{"transaction_id": "txn-1234",
 "created_by": "operator-alias",
 "created_at": "2026-05-15T14:23:00Z",
 "artifacts": [
   {"path": "configs.tar.gz", "sha256": "<hex>", "owner": "platform-ops"},
   {"path": "telemetry-90d.parquet", "sha256": "<hex>", "owner": "observability"}
 ]
}

Note: the above JSON example is for human-readability in this handbook; the actual manifest is written as a single-line compact JSON during export.

Appendix B: recommended timeline for a typical deal (30-60 days)
----------------------------------------------------------------
- Days 0-7: Transaction letter and scope definition
- Days 8-14: Approvals and operator scheduling
- Days 15-28: Evidence collection, redaction, and security verification
- Days 29-35: Recipient verification and acceptance testing
- Days 36-60: Post-handoff follow-ups, retention decisions, and closing paperwork

Contact and escalation
---------------------
For questions or to schedule an evidence export rehearsal, contact: security@redwood.ai (primary) and legal@redwood.ai (secondary).
